# Indicateur d'activité uniforme : conception UX

Date : 2026-11-06, mis à jour le 2026-11-06 avec les décisions de l'utilisateur (`stories.md`, tableau « Décisions tranchées », D7 à D10). Entrées : `brief.md`, `stories.md` (dont « Faisabilité (architect) »), `research.md`, Rules 111/118/121/122/125/128/139, `internal/ui/theme/` (`icons.go`, `iconcolors.go`, `colors.go`, `manager.go`).
Tout le texte d'interface cité (footer, aide) est en anglais US (Rule 129) ; le reste du document est en français.

**Questions bloquantes : aucune.** Les choix de glyphes, de phase éteinte, de fréquence, de `restarting`, d'`exited` code 0 et de conteneur `running` sont **tranchés** (§6). Deux points restent à confirmer (§6). Les hypothèses sont marquées `Hypothèse :`.

## 0. Principes retenus

1. **Forme de base ● (imposée).** Tous les états sont des cercles ou des glyphes ronds de même emprise (`●` `○` `◴` `◐` `◕` `◉` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖`, blocs Unicode « Geometric Shapes » et « Mathematical Operators », pas des Nerd Fonts). Conséquence utile : la pastille ne dépend pas d'un Nerd Font, ce qui allège le backlog §3.98 pour cette colonne (les icônes de repos, elles, en dépendent encore).
2. **Un état = un glyphe unique dans toute l'application, plus une couleur.** L'unicité est globale (test de A-16 : pas deux sens pour un même point de code). La lisibilité, elle, se juge entre états qui apparaissent *dans la même vue* (matrice §2.4).
3. **La couleur est redondante partout.** Jamais deux états qui ne diffèrent que par la teinte.
4. **Rouge jamais clignotant.** Seule la pastille « en cours » bouge (WCAG 2.3.1 : le seuil « flash rouge » ne peut donc pas s'appliquer).
5. **Cellule = texte brut d'un seul glyphe** (Rule 122) ; `datatable` complète à `IconColumnWidth` (2). Le `Cell` ne met pas d'espace final lui-même : `datatable` mesure avec `runewidth`, et ces glyphes sont « ambigus » en largeur Est-asiatique (2 cellules dans un terminal CJK) ; un glyphe + espace y mesurerait 3 et serait tronqué. Voir §5.

## 1. Tableau des états

### 1.1 Alphabet global

Couleurs : alias **fermés**, assignés dans `ApplyTheme` (comme `ColorFooter*`), pointant sur des couleurs existantes de `colors.go`. Noms proposés pour l'API ; les valeurs sont des noms existants.

| Alias proposé | Pointe sur (`colors.go`) | Valeur par défaut (Catppuccin) |
|---|---|---|
| `ColorActivityRunning` | `ColorSecondary` | `#b4befe` (lavande) |
| `ColorActivityNeutral` | `ColorText` | `#cdd6f4` |
| `ColorActivitySuspended` | `ColorFooterWarn` (= `ColorSeverityMedium`) | `#fab387` (orange) |
| `ColorActivityFailed` | `ColorFooterError` (= `ColorSeverityCritical`) | `#f38ba8` (rouge) |

Pourquoi lavande pour « en cours » : ni vert (exclu), ni jaune (`ColorHighlight` = focus de formulaire, Rule 120), ni rouge/orange ; c'est déjà la couleur « actif » (onglet, en-tête), donc le sens est cohérent. `ColorDim` (`#585b70`) n'est **pas** utilisé : voir §2, il tombe à environ 2,5:1 sur le fond et 1,9:1 sous la sélection normale.

| Glyphe | Sens | Alias | Clignote |
|---|---|---|---|
| `●` (allumé) / `○` (éteint) | opération en cours | `ColorActivityRunning` | oui, 1 Hz |
| `◴` | en file | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
| `⊗` | échec (opération échouée, conteneur `dead` ou `exited` non nul) | `ColorActivityFailed` | non, jamais |
| `◐` | suspendu : agent `idle`, conteneur `paused` | `ColorActivitySuspended` | non |
| `◕` | conteneur `restarting` | `ColorActivitySuspended` | non (fixe, tranché) |
| `◉` | terminé, **et rien d'autre** : job `done`, agent `done` | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
| `⊘` | annulé (job `cancelled`) | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
| `⊖` | sans action : job `skipped`, conteneur `exited` code 0 | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
| `◌` | inconnu / pas encore démarré : agent `unknown`, conteneur `created` | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
| repos | icône habituelle de la ligne (rôle `IconRole*` existant) ou cellule vide. **Un conteneur `running` est au repos** : état nominal (Rule 122), aucune pastille | rôle existant | non |
| mode « sans mouvement » | `●` fixe (la phase allumée) | `ColorActivityRunning` | non |

`●` et `○` sont réservés à « en cours » : aucun autre état ne les emploie, donc une capture figée sur l'une ou l'autre phase reste sans ambiguïté. `◉` est réservé à « terminé » (job `done`, agent `done`). Glyphes, phase éteinte `○` et mode `●` fixe : tranchés (D7).

### 1.2 Par vue : glyphe, texte équivalent au footer

Le footer porte le glyphe d'état en préfixe, en texte brut (Rule 128 interdit la couleur propre ; le préfixe relie le texte à la pastille sans passer par la couleur). Phrases construites par un seul constructeur (A-05, critère 8). **Exception : un conteneur `running` n'a pas de pastille, son footer n'a donc pas de glyphe en préfixe** (D8). Libellés validés par l'utilisateur (D10).

| État | Glyphe (allumé / éteint) | Couleur | Clignote | Footer (ligne sélectionnée, niveau `Status`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opération en cours | `●` / `○` | Running | oui | `● Scanning ~/w/app/api` ; `● Syncing ~/w/app/web` ; `● Removing nginx:1.27` |
| En file | `◴` / `◴` | Neutral | non | `◴ Queued: scan ~/w/app/api` |
| Échec | `⊗` / `⊗` | Failed | non | `⊗ ~/w/app/api: last scan failed — trivy could not pull the database` |
| `:jobs` done | `◉` | Neutral | non | `◉ Scan of ~/w/app/api finished 2 min ago` |
| `:jobs` failed | `⊗` | Failed | non | comme « Échec » |
| `:jobs` cancelled | `⊘` | Neutral | non | `⊘ Scan of ~/w/app/api was cancelled` |
| `:jobs` skipped | `⊖` | Neutral | non | `⊖ Scan of ~/w/app/api skipped — result already cached` |
| `:jobs` en cours / en file | `●`/`○` ; `◴` | Running ; Neutral | oui ; non | comme ci-dessus |
| `:agent-usage` running | `●` / `○` | Running | oui | `● Agent running — last transcript line 4 s ago` |
| `:agent-usage` idle | `◐` | Suspended | non | `◐ Agent idle — no transcript line for 7 min` |
| `:agent-usage` done | `◉` | Neutral | non | `◉ Agent done — ran 12 min` |
| `:agent-usage` unknown | `◌` | Neutral | non | `◌ Agent state unknown — transcript has no end marker` |
| Conteneur running | (aucune pastille : icône habituelle) | — | non | `Running since 3 hr ago` (sans glyphe en préfixe) |
| Conteneur restarting | `◕` | Suspended | non | `◕ Restarting — 4 restarts, last exit code 1` |
| Conteneur paused | `◐` | Suspended | non | `◐ Paused` |
| Conteneur created | `◌` | Neutral | non | `◌ Created, never started` |
| Conteneur exited (code ≠ 0) | `⊗` | Failed | non | `⊗ Exited with code 137 — 5 min ago` |
| Conteneur exited (code 0) | `⊖` | Neutral | non | `⊖ Exited cleanly (code 0) — 5 min ago` |
| Conteneur dead | `⊗` | Failed | non | `⊗ Dead — the engine could not stop it cleanly` |
| Action instantanée sur conteneur (stop, kill, remove) | `●` / `○` | Running | oui | `● Stopping web-1` |

Hypothèse : les libellés exacts (« last transcript line 4 s ago ») dépendent des données disponibles dans chaque vue ; seule la structure `glyphe + phrase` est prescrite.

Priorité sur une ligne, déjà décidée : **en cours > en file > échec > état observé > repos** (une seule fonction, `indicator.Resolve`). Quand un échec est masqué par une opération en cours, le footer l'ajoute en suffixe : `● Scanning ~/w/app/api · earlier failure: sync (see :jobs)`.

### 1.3 Choix tranchés (décision 7, 2026-11-06)

Les options étudiées avant la décision sont abandonnées ; il ne reste que le choix et sa raison.

- **Phase éteinte du clignotement : `○`, même couleur lavande.** Une capture figée se lit « quelque chose est là, en mouvement », jamais « rien » ; la couleur ne change pas (pas de scintillement de teinte) ; le contraste reste celui de l'état allumé (environ 7:1 sur la sélection). Écartés : `●` atténué en `ColorDim` (proche d'une cellule vide, échoue 3:1 : environ 2,5:1 sur le fond, 1,9:1 sous le curseur), `●` en `ColorText` (confondable avec un état terminé).
- **Conteneur `restarting` : `◕` orange fixe.** C'est un état observé, pas une opération lancée par DevDesk ; pas de dépendance au signal `WantsBlink` pour ce cas ; un `restarting` en boucle de crash change plus vite que le sondage docker, donc un clignotement synchronisé sur le tick serait trompeur ; `○` reste réservé à « en cours ».
- **« En file » : `◴` statique, `ColorActivityNeutral`.** Une file n'est pas une activité ; faire clignoter ce qui attend fait croire que ça avance, et un lot de 12 scans compterait 11 clignotants de plus sans information.
- **Conteneur `running` : aucune pastille** (D8). L'état nominal ne se colore pas (Rule 122, « color discipline ») ; la ligne garde son icône habituelle, et la pastille ne signale que ce qui s'écarte du nominal.

## 2. Test de lisibilité

Hypothèse : les rapports de contraste ci-dessous sont des calculs à la main (luminance relative WCAG) sur les valeurs par défaut Catppuccin (fond `#1e1e2e`, sélection `#313244`) ; `theme/contrast_test.go` doit les confirmer (A-01, critère 6).

### 2.1 Contraste des couleurs de pastille (critère WCAG 1.4.11, seuil 3:1)

| Couleur | Sur fond `#1e1e2e` | Sur sélection `#313244` |
|---|---|---|
| Running `#b4befe` | environ 9:1 | environ 7:1 |
| Neutral `#cdd6f4` | environ 11:1 | environ 8:1 |

### 2.2 Les quatre épreuves

| # | Épreuve | Résultat | Où ça échoue, et le correctif |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | **Sans couleur** (`NO_COLOR`, monochrome) : dix glyphes tous distincts | passe, avec une paire faible | `●` contre `◉` : un point plein contre un anneau à point, proches à petite taille dans certaines polices. Ils se croisent dans `:jobs` et `:agent-usage` (en cours contre terminé), pas dans containers (un conteneur `running` n'a pas de pastille, D8). Correctifs : (1) le clignotement les sépare dès qu'on regarde deux secondes ; (2) le footer écrit l'état. L'utilisateur les distingue dans son terminal : **pas de repli `✓`** (D7). |
| b | **Sans mouvement** (capture figée, ou réglage `static`) | passe | La phase éteinte `○` est un anneau lavande, réservé : un cliché pris à l'instant « éteint » se lit « en cours ». En mode `static`, `●` fixe : le seul état qui bouge perd son mouvement mais garde glyphe et couleur, tous deux uniques parmi les états de la même vue. |
| c | **Daltonisme rouge/vert** (deutéranopie, protanopie) | passe | Le thème n'emploie aucun vert. Rouge `#f38ba8` et orange `#fab387` convergent vers des jaunes-gris proches : ils se distinguent par le glyphe (`⊗` contre `◐`/`◕`), c'est la raison d'être de la règle. Lavande et texte convergent aussi vers des gris-bleu : `●`/`○` contre `◉` les sépare. |
| d | **Sous le curseur, sélection normale** | passe | La Rule 118 révisée (§3.72) garde la couleur de chaque cellule, repeinte sur `ColorTableLineSelected` ; le gras est ajouté. Toutes les couleurs de pastille dépassent 3:1 dessus (§2.1). Le clignotement continue : la phase est lue au rendu. |
| d' | **Sous une ligne colorée en entier** (erreur de containers, `busy`, sévérité) | passe, par le glyphe | La couleur de la pastille tombe (fond plein `ColorError`, texte `ColorBlack`). Le glyphe reste : `⊗` noir sur rouge, et pour l'action en cours `●`/`○` qui alterne dans le texte de la cellule (raisonnement de `rowLine` pour `busy`, Q6 de l'architect). |

### 2.3 Cas où l'état est ambigu au seul coup d'œil, et réponse

- Repos (icône de ligne) contre `◌` (vide, créé, inconnu) : l'icône de repos est un glyphe Nerd Font de type de ligne, `◌` est un anneau en pointillé : distincts. Si la vue n'a pas d'icône, le repos est une cellule vide (jamais `◌`).
- `⊗` rouge pour `exited` non nul et pour `dead` : même glyphe, sens « cassé ». Le statut texte du conteneur (colonne Status) et le footer distinguent les deux.

### 2.4 Matrice de coexistence (ce qui doit rester distinguable dans une même vue)

| Vue | États qui coexistent |
|---|---|
| `:jobs` | `●`/`○`, `◴`, `⊗`, `◉`, `⊘`, `⊖` |
| `ws`, `:sec`, OCI | `●`/`○`, `◴`, `⊗`, icône de repos |
| `:agent-usage` | `●`/`○`, `◐`, `◉`, `◌` |
| containers | icône de repos (conteneur `running`), `◕`, `◐`, `◌`, `⊗`, `⊖`, `●`/`○` (action instantanée) |

Chaque ligne a des glyphes deux à deux distincts ; la seule paire faible est `●` contre `◉` (a), qui ne se croise plus dans containers.

### 3.6 Footer : ligne en cours, ligne en erreur (Rule 128)

Précédence : error > warn > info > status. Un détail de ligne est de niveau `Status` (sans minuteur, recalculé à chaque trame), composé « détail de ligne · progression globale ». Le détail est tronqué d'abord (Rule 124 : la hauteur ne change pas).

Ligne en cours (`ws`, ligne `api` sélectionnée, sync de 12 dépôts) :

```
(blanc)
        ● Syncing ~/w/app/api · 3/12 repositories
```

Niveau `Status`, texte de couleur ordinaire. Pas de spinner de footer ici : la pastille bouge déjà sur la ligne ; un spinner doublerait le mouvement.

Ligne en erreur, en trois temps :

| Temps | Niveau | Texte | Couleur |
|---|---|---|---|
| t = 0 à 3 s (l'échec arrive) | `Error`, avec minuteur | `Failed to scan ~/w/app/web — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterError`, gras |
| t > 3 s, ligne `web` sélectionnée | `Status`, persistant | `⊗ ~/w/app/web: last scan failed — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterInfo`, normal |
| t > 3 s, autre ligne sélectionnée | `Status` | le détail de cette ligne, ou la progression globale seule | idem |

La pastille rouge fixe persiste jusqu'à la prochaine tentative sur la ligne ; seul le texte de footer passe de l'événement à l'état (décision de l'architect, Q4). Si une opération est en cours sur la même ligne, l'échec masqué est en suffixe (§1.2). Si un autre `Error` arrive pendant les 3 s, il prend le pas (précédence inchangée).

## 4. Fréquence et « en file »

**Tranché (D7) : 1 Hz (500 ms allumé, 500 ms éteint), phase déduite de l'horloge.**

| | 1 Hz (recommandé) | 2 Hz |
|---|---|---|
| WCAG 2.3.1 (≤ 3 flashs/s) | 1 flash/s : marge de 3 | 2 flashs/s : sous le seuil, marge de 1,5 |
| Perception | pouls calme, ne distrait pas pendant la lecture d'un tableau | réveille l'œil, se lit comme une alerte |
| Coût (SSH) | une réécriture de cellule par ligne par seconde | le double |
| Cadence du tick routeur | 500 ms (déjà prévue par l'architect) | 250 ms |
| Détection de l'état gelé | un blocage de plus de 1 s se voit | idem, plus vite |

Justification complémentaire : la surface qui clignote est minuscule (une cellule par ligne), la variation de luminance est modeste (anneau contre disque, même couleur), et rien ne clignote en rouge. Toutes les pastilles clignotent **en phase** : un décalage entre lignes créerait un effet de vague qui augmente le flash perçu. La phase vient du temps du message de tick (`on = (t.UnixMilli() / 500) % 2 == 0`) : survit à un changement de cadence, testable. 2 Hz resterait une constante à changer si le pilote la jugeait trop lente (le premier point de contrôle peut le rouvrir).

**« En file » : statique** (`◴`, `ColorActivityNeutral`). Voir §1.3. Passage `◴` à `●`/`○` à la prise en charge ; le tick démarre alors, une seule fois.

## 5. Cas limites

1. **Plusieurs pastilles simultanées dans une vue.** Toutes en phase, pas de plafond. Un lot de N scans donne 1 en cours + (N−1) en file : un seul clignotant (le tick est partagé) et N−1 `◴` fixes ; la progression globale (« 3/12 ») reste au footer. Si 50 % des lignes visibles clignotent, la surface reste faible et la fréquence est de 1 Hz ; pas de réduction supplémentaire à prévoir. Le réglage `app.motion: static` reste la sortie (A-02).
2. **Ligne en cours et en échec à la fois** : priorité décidée ; l'échec réapparaît à la fin de l'opération, sa clé n'ayant pas changé. Footer avec suffixe (§1.2).
3. **Largeur des glyphes.** `●` `○` `◐` `◕` `◴` `◉` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` sont, pour la plupart, de largeur « ambiguë » (la largeur de `◴` est à vérifier dans la rangée de test) (1 cellule en locale occidentale, 2 dans un terminal configuré en Est-asiatique) et certains Nerd Fonts les élargissent. `IconColumnWidth` = 2 couvre les deux cas, à condition que le `Cell` renvoie **le glyphe seul** et que `datatable` complète à 2 avec `runewidth`. Test à ajouter : la Rule 116 tient avec `runewidth.EastAsianWidth = true`. Un glyphe de 2 cellules colle alors au texte voisin : accepté, la colonne n'a pas de marge de plus.
4. **Terminal sans Nerd Font** (note seulement, hors périmètre, voir backlog §3.98). La pastille n'est pas affectée (glyphes Unicode standard), contrairement aux icônes de repos, qui s'afficheront comme des carrés. Mais certains polices de console (ex. Consolas sous Windows, hypothèse non vérifiée) n'ont pas `◴` `◕` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` et les substituent par une police de repli, donc parfois plus larges. À consigner pour §3.98 ; l'utilisateur a confirmé le rendu dans son terminal (D7) ; les autres terminaux restent une note.
5. **`NO_COLOR` et terminaux 16 couleurs** : les quatre alias retombent sur des couleurs distinctes ou sur la couleur par défaut ; l'unicité des glyphes garantit la lecture. Aucun cas ne repose sur la teinte.
6. **Conteneur `exited` 0** : `⊖` neutre, tranché (D7). Un arrêt volontaire n'a rien à corriger ; rouge partout diluerait la couleur d'alerte (Rule 122 « color discipline ») et noierait les vrais `exited` non nuls et les `dead`.
7. **Rafraîchissement périodique** (métriques containers, ports en direct, lecture agents de 2 s) : ne déclenche aucun clignotement (donnée).
8. **Action `docker stop` instantanée** : la pastille `●`/`○` apparaît par l'état `busy` (priorité « en cours »), puis l'icône habituelle (conteneur `running`) ou le glyphe d'état observé revient au prochain sondage ; un échec reste au footer (non-objectif).
9. **Focus de formulaire.** `IconCircleSmall` (``, Nerd Font) signale le champ actif dans les formulaires. C'est une forme proche de `●` mais dans un autre écran, jamais dans une table : pas de collision, à rappeler dans l'aide.
10. **Ligne sans icône de repos** : cellule vide de largeur `IconColumnWidth`, jamais `◌`.

### Libellé de la légende de l'aide `?` (Rule 114, anglais US)

Une seule source dérivée de la table de glyphes (A-01 absorbe A-15). Base, présente dans chaque vue migrée :

```
Title: Activity indicator
Description: The first column shows what is happening on a row. The glyph carries the
meaning; the color repeats it. Nothing here relies on color alone.

  ●  ○   Running (blinks). Pauses to a steady ● when motion is off.
  ◴      Queued, waiting to start.
  ⊗      Failed. Stays until the next attempt on that row; the footer gives the cause.
  (icon) Idle: the row's usual icon, or an empty cell.

The footer describes the selected row's state in words.
Turn the blinking off with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg.
```

Libellés **validés** (D10), à une réserve : la fin de la dernière phrase (« or in :cfg ») suppose que `app.motion` est modifiable dans la vue de configuration. **À confirmer** (architect, comme `app.gauge_glyph`) ; sinon retirer « or in :cfg ».

Extension propre à `:jobs` : `◉ done · ⊘ cancelled · ⊖ skipped`.
Extension propre à `:agent-usage` : `◐ idle (no activity for 5 min) · ◉ done · ◌ unknown`.
Extension propre à la liste de clone de l'explorer : `◉ cloned (clone list) · ⊖ already on disk, or not started (cancelled) (clone list)`. Plusieurs lignes peuvent clignoter en même temps (les clones tournent en parallèle, `forge.pull.parallel_jobs`) : chaque clone en cours clignote, les autres restent `◴`.
Extension propre aux containers : `◕ restarting · ◐ paused · ◌ created · ⊖ exited (code 0) · ⊗ exited (non-zero code) or dead · ●/○ an action (stop, kill, remove) is running`. Pas de ligne `running` : un conteneur qui tourne montre son icône habituelle (D8).

En tant qu'utilisateur de la vue containers, je veux voir l'état observé de chaque conteneur qui n'est pas nominal dans la première colonne, afin de repérer ceux qui redémarrent, sont en pause, arrêtés ou morts, sans spinner par ligne.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné la table des conteneurs, quand elle s'affiche, alors la première colonne est la pastille, calculée par la vue depuis les états observés par docker ; le spinner de ligne et l'`AdvanceSpinner` sont supprimés.
2. Étant donné un conteneur `running` (état nominal, Rule 122), quand il s'affiche, alors il n'a **aucune pastille** : la ligne montre son icône habituelle (D8) ; `◉` n'est pas utilisé ici. Hypothèse: l'icône de repos est l'icône de type de conteneur ; son rôle `IconRole*` est à préciser à l'implémentation.
3. Étant donné les autres états, quand on compare leurs glyphes, alors ils sont tous différents entre sens différents (test) : `restarting` `◕` orange fixe ; `paused` `◐` orange fixe ; `created` `◌` neutre ; `exited` code ≠ 0 `⊗` rouge fixe ; `exited` code 0 `⊖` neutre ; `dead` `⊗` rouge fixe.
4. Étant donné une action instantanée (`docker stop`, `kill`, `remove`) en cours, quand elle s'exécute, alors la pastille `●`/`○` apparaît (`busy`, priorité « en cours », signal `WantsBlink`), puis l'icône ou le glyphe d'état observé revient au sondage suivant ; son échec reste au footer (non-objectif).
5. Étant donné les filtres d'état `r p s t z` (Rule 111), quand ils changent, alors leur comportement et leur vocabulaire ne changent pas.
6. Étant donné un rafraîchissement périodique des métriques, quand il s'exécute, alors aucun clignotement n'est déclenché (donnée, pas opération) ; `restarting` ne clignote pas (état observé).
7. Étant donné une ligne sélectionnée, quand le footer s'affiche, alors il détaille l'état (`ux.md` §1.2) ; pour un conteneur `running`, « Running since 3 hr ago » **sans glyphe en préfixe**.
8. Terminal de 60 colonnes : Rule 116 tient ; les jauges CPU/mémoire (`Cut`/`TailStyle`) ne sont pas touchées ; l'aide `?` décrit les glyphes de la légende de base et l'extension containers (`◕ restarting · ◐ paused · ◌ created · ⊖ exited (code 0) · ⊗ exited (non-zero code) or dead · ●/○ an action (stop, kill, remove) is running`, sans `◉ running`) et remplace l'aide existante (`view.go`).

1	# DEVDESK-150 (A-12) — netdiag Ports: activity column for the kill
2	
3	Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-12. UX: `ux.md` §1 (glyphs), §5 (legend).
4	Worktree: `.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-150-netdiag-ports-activity` (base `e037b2f`).
5	Pattern: DEVDESK-146 (OCI images, the closest twin: a `busy` action, `MarkBusy`/`ClearBusy`,
6	reported as `Observed: Running` through `components.DescribeRow`), DEVDESK-148/149 (guard, help).
7	
8	**What makes this story small.** The Ports table has no registry run at all: its only row
9	operation is `K` (SIGKILL), held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID. `datatable` already
10	writes the precedence "busy ⇒ `indicator.Running`" once (`render.go::indicatorState`), so the
11	view only adds an `IndicatorColumn` whose own state is always `Idle`. `jobs.ChangedMsg`,
12	`jobs.ForgetTarget`, `FailureEvent` and the failure memory are **not used**: nothing here goes
13	through the registry, and the kill failure stays a footer `Error` (criterion 1, D5: there is no
14	kill kind to remember).
15	
16	Out of scope: `H`, the Diagnostics (checks) and Interfaces tables, the Forward tab, `internal/ports`.
17	
18	## Finding in the current code (fixed by the story itself)
19	
20	`portsSpinnerTickMsg` is not routed by `netdiag.Model.Update` (`update.go:90` lists
21	`portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg` only): the tick lands in the fall-through and
22	is dropped, so in production the row spinner shows frame 0 and never turns.
23	`TestTheKillSpinnerTickStopsWhenTheKillLands` calls `handleSpinnerTick` directly and does not see it.
24	The story deletes the chain; no separate bug.
25	
26	## Blocking questions (user)
27	
28	| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
29	|---|---|---|---|
30	| Q1 | **Open question 4 of `stories.md`: a network test that fails** (TCP refused, invalid TLS) — row result or remembered operation failure? | **A** result: it stays in the Verdict column of the checks table, nothing changes there; the red dot is reserved for an operation that failed (criterion 4 as written) · **B** remembered failure: a `⊗` and the failure memory for a diagnostic, which needs a column on the checks table, a kind in the registry, and is no longer an S story | **A**: the Verdict already says FAIL in red with its reason; a `⊗` on top would say the same thing twice, and "the check could not look" (UNKNOWN) is a result too. The plan is written for A (criterion 4 = a regression test). B would be a new story. |
31	| Q2 | **What the State cell shows during a kill.** Today the State cell is replaced by the spinner (§3.22: "the row must not show the state the signal is about to change"; `TestAKillSpinsTheSocketState` pins it). With the dot in column 0 that replacement goes (`StatusColumn` is a retired mechanism). | **A** State keeps its text, dimmed like every busy row (`datatable.cellStyle` busy branch, no view code; same as OCI images after DEVDESK-146) · **B** State reads `killing` (dim) while busy, from a `Cell` that checks `IsBusy` (the view reads the busy map in a cell: a second path to the same fact) · **C** State blank while busy | **A**: the dot says "in progress", the dim says "ceasing to be true" (the datatable comment's wording), and one alphabet with OCI. It reverses the letter of §3.22 (LISTEN visible, dim) but keeps its intent. |
32	
33	## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)
34	
35	- H1 **Column 0** = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(ports.Socket) indicator.State { return indicator.Idle }, nil, nil)`:
36	  no rest icon (the row has none), so an idle row shows an empty two-cell column. A busy row is
37	  `Running` through `datatable`'s precedence: every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○` (today's
38	  "every row of that process spins" kept).
39	- H2 **The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`** handled by `netdiag.Model.Update`:
40	  `m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`, nothing rebuilt. **The footers' spinner frames
41	  are not touched**: the Diagnostics run and the Interfaces load keep their own `spinner.TickMsg`
42	  chain (D2, criterion 5).
43	- H3 **`WantsBlink()`** (router's `BlinkingView`) on `*netdiag.Model` = `len(m.portsModel.table.BusyLabels()) > 0`,
44	  whatever the active tab (a level; the router only frames the view on screen; a kill lasts a moment).
45	- H4 **Per-row footer** (A-05): `PortsModel.statusLine()` adds `Detail` = `components.DescribeRow(RowQuery{Observed: indicator.Running, ObservedText: label}).Detail`
46	  when the selected row's PID is busy (label = the existing `"Killing <process> (<pid>)"`), zero
47	  otherwise. Text/Level (stale error, paused) unchanged and placed after the detail by
48	  `RowStatusLine`. At 60 columns this is where the process name is readable (PID and Process
49	  columns are dropped there).
50	- H5 **Kill outcomes unchanged**: success `Info` "Process N terminated", failure `Error`
51	  `killFailureMessage` (§3.49, D5), `ClearBusy` on both; the row returns to rest (no `⊗`).
52	  `K` stays lit on a busy row (Rule 130: an operation in progress is not a reason to grey);
53	  `Already killing PID N` warning kept.
54	- H6 **The periodic refresh never blinks** (criterion 3): `SetItems` does not touch `busy`; a
55	  refresh with nothing busy leaves every column-0 cell empty and `WantsBlink()` false.
56	- H7 **Scan scope of the guard**: the I/O commands (`fetchPortsCmd`, `portsTickCmd`,
57	  `killProcessCmd`, `defaultPortsRefresh`, `portsFetchTimeout`) move to a new
58	  `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_commands.go`, **not scanned**, exactly like OCI's `commands.go`
59	  (its refresh `tea.Tick` is data, not a row animation). Scanned: `ports_model.go`,
60	  `ports_activity.go`, `header.go`, `update.go`. `forward_model.go` (its own refresh tick) and the
61	  other tabs are not scanned (not migrated). Alternative rejected: an entry in
62	  `declaredViewTicks`, documented as "empty today, may only shrink".
63	- H8 **Guard footer seed**: the seed must not read the real socket table nor kill anything. It
64	  needs an exported way to hand rows to the view: `func NewPortsDataMsg(sockets []ports.Socket) tea.Msg`
65	  in `ports_commands.go` (returns the unexported `portsDataMsg`; no rename, no test churn). The
66	  seed drives the view's `Update` directly (not the router: the Init `Cmd` and the kill `Cmd` are

# DEVDESK-150 (A-12) — netdiag Ports: activity column for the kill

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-12. UX: `ux.md` §1 (glyphs), §5 (legend).
Worktree: `.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-150-netdiag-ports-activity` (base `e037b2f`).
Pattern: DEVDESK-146 (OCI images, the closest twin: a `busy` action, `MarkBusy`/`ClearBusy`,
reported as `Observed: Running` through `components.DescribeRow`), DEVDESK-148/149 (guard, help).

**What makes this story small.** The Ports table has no registry run at all: its only row
operation is `K` (SIGKILL), held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID. `datatable` already
writes the precedence "busy ⇒ `indicator.Running`" once (`render.go::indicatorState`), so the
view only adds an `IndicatorColumn` whose own state is always `Idle`. `jobs.ChangedMsg`,
`jobs.ForgetTarget`, `FailureEvent` and the failure memory are **not used**: nothing here goes
through the registry, and the kill failure stays a footer `Error` (criterion 1, D5: there is no
kill kind to remember).

Out of scope: `H`, the Diagnostics (checks) and Interfaces tables, the Forward tab, `internal/ports`.

## Finding in the current code (fixed by the story itself)

`portsSpinnerTickMsg` is not routed by `netdiag.Model.Update` (`update.go:90` lists
`portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg` only): the tick lands in the fall-through and
is dropped, so in production the row spinner shows frame 0 and never turns.
`TestTheKillSpinnerTickStopsWhenTheKillLands` calls `handleSpinnerTick` directly and does not see it.
The story deletes the chain; no separate bug.

## Blocking questions (user)

| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **Open question 4 of `stories.md`: a network test that fails** (TCP refused, invalid TLS) — row result or remembered operation failure? | **A** result: it stays in the Verdict column of the checks table, nothing changes there; the red dot is reserved for an operation that failed (criterion 4 as written) · **B** remembered failure: a `⊗` and the failure memory for a diagnostic, which needs a column on the checks table, a kind in the registry, and is no longer an S story | **A**: the Verdict already says FAIL in red with its reason; a `⊗` on top would say the same thing twice, and "the check could not look" (UNKNOWN) is a result too. The plan is written for A (criterion 4 = a regression test). B would be a new story. |
| Q2 | **What the State cell shows during a kill.** Today the State cell is replaced by the spinner (§3.22: "the row must not show the state the signal is about to change"; `TestAKillSpinsTheSocketState` pins it). With the dot in column 0 that replacement goes (`StatusColumn` is a retired mechanism). | **A** State keeps its text, dimmed like every busy row (`datatable.cellStyle` busy branch, no view code; same as OCI images after DEVDESK-146) · **B** State reads `killing` (dim) while busy, from a `Cell` that checks `IsBusy` (the view reads the busy map in a cell: a second path to the same fact) · **C** State blank while busy | **A**: the dot says "in progress", the dim says "ceasing to be true" (the datatable comment's wording), and one alphabet with OCI. It reverses the letter of §3.22 (LISTEN visible, dim) but keeps its intent. |

## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)

- H1 **Column 0** = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(ports.Socket) indicator.State { return indicator.Idle }, nil, nil)`:
  no rest icon (the row has none), so an idle row shows an empty two-cell column. A busy row is
  `Running` through `datatable`'s precedence: every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○` (today's
  "every row of that process spins" kept).
- H2 **The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`** handled by `netdiag.Model.Update`:
  `m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`, nothing rebuilt. **The footers' spinner frames
  are not touched**: the Diagnostics run and the Interfaces load keep their own `spinner.TickMsg`
  chain (D2, criterion 5).
- H3 **`WantsBlink()`** (router's `BlinkingView`) on `*netdiag.Model` = `len(m.portsModel.table.BusyLabels()) > 0`,
  whatever the active tab (a level; the router only frames the view on screen; a kill lasts a moment).
- H4 **Per-row footer** (A-05): `PortsModel.statusLine()` adds `Detail` = `components.DescribeRow(RowQuery{Observed: indicator.Running, ObservedText: label}).Detail`
  when the selected row's PID is busy (label = the existing `"Killing <process> (<pid>)"`), zero
  otherwise. Text/Level (stale error, paused) unchanged and placed after the detail by
  `RowStatusLine`. At 60 columns this is where the process name is readable (PID and Process
  columns are dropped there).
- H5 **Kill outcomes unchanged**: success `Info` "Process N terminated", failure `Error`
  `killFailureMessage` (§3.49, D5), `ClearBusy` on both; the row returns to rest (no `⊗`).
  `K` stays lit on a busy row (Rule 130: an operation in progress is not a reason to grey);
  `Already killing PID N` warning kept.
- H6 **The periodic refresh never blinks** (criterion 3): `SetItems` does not touch `busy`; a
  refresh with nothing busy leaves every column-0 cell empty and `WantsBlink()` false.
- H7 **Scan scope of the guard**: the I/O commands (`fetchPortsCmd`, `portsTickCmd`,
  `killProcessCmd`, `defaultPortsRefresh`, `portsFetchTimeout`) move to a new
  `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_commands.go`, **not scanned**, exactly like OCI's `commands.go`
  (its refresh `tea.Tick` is data, not a row animation). Scanned: `ports_model.go`,
  `ports_activity.go`, `header.go`, `update.go`. `forward_model.go` (its own refresh tick) and the
  other tabs are not scanned (not migrated). Alternative rejected: an entry in
  `declaredViewTicks`, documented as "empty today, may only shrink".

  needs an exported way to hand rows to the view: `func NewPortsDataMsg(sockets []ports.Socket) tea.Msg`

  seed drives the view's `Update` directly (not the router: the Init `Cmd` and the kill `Cmd` are
  never executed), with a PID that cannot exist on Linux (`"4194305"` > `pid_max`).

276	// survives the selected row too, where neither Style nor TailStyle is
277	// consulted at all (Rule 122). DropFirst because a gauge sits where the number
278	// it illustrates is, in the middle of the table: left to position alone it
279	// would outlive the I/O counters to its right, which is the opposite of what a

281	//

283	// the track fixed — which is what lets the empty portion of an idle
284	// container's bar stay the same colour as a busy one's, rather than
285	// inheriting whatever the fill's own colour happens to be that row.
286	//

288	// neither colour is consulted, see above — the bar renders as one uniform
289	// block and says nothing on its own. The number beside it is what survives
290	// there; that trade is why the number is never dropped even at the narrowest
291	// width the table allows.

296	func gaugeColumn(scale string, pct func(docker.Container) float64) datatable.Column[docker.Container] {
297		return datatable.Column[docker.Container]{
298			Title: scale, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: theme.GaugeWidth,
299			Optional: true, DropFirst: true,
300			Cell: func(c docker.Container) string {
301				if c.State != "running" {
302					return "-"
303				}
304				return theme.Gauge(pct(c), theme.GaugeWidth)
305			},
306			Style: func(c docker.Container) lipgloss.Style {
307				if c.State != "running" {
308					// A placeholder is dim, like every other "-" in this table.
309					return theme.DimStyle
310				}
311				return theme.LoadTextStyle(pct(c))
312			},
313			Cut: func(c docker.Container) int {
314				if c.State != "running" {
315					// The whole "-" belongs to TailStyle: 0 fill cells.
316					return 0
317				}
318				return theme.GaugeFillWidth(pct(c), theme.GaugeWidth)
319			},
320			TailStyle: func(c docker.Container) lipgloss.Style {
321				if c.State != "running" {
322					return theme.DimStyle
323				}
324				return theme.GaugeTrackStyle()
325			},
326		}
327	}
328	
329	// containerStateStyle colours the status column by the state its glyph shows.
330	//
331	// A running container is left in the default text colour rather than painted
332	// green. Almost every row is running, so colouring them would put a colour on
333	// the whole table and a signal on none of it — the colour is here to pick out
334	// the containers that stopped, or that are on their way somewhere.
335	func containerStateStyle(c docker.Container) lipgloss.Style {
336		switch c.State {
337		case "exited", "dead":
338			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
339		case "paused":
340			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
341		case "created", "restarting":
342			return lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
343		default:
344			// No opinion here: the table sets the theme's text color.
345			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
346		}
347	}
348	
349	// containerSelectedStyles paints the selected row as an error when the
350	// container is not coming back on its own. It is the whole of what
351	// refreshSelectionStyle used to do, minus its replay of filter-then-sort to
352	// find out what the cursor was on.
353	func containerSelectedStyles(c docker.Container) table.Styles {
354		if c.State == "exited" || c.State == "dead" {
355			return theme.TableStylesForState("error")
356		}
357		return theme.TableStylesForState("normal")
358	}
359	
360	// The state filter tokens (Rule 136). They replace `a`, a two-position switch
361	// — running only, or everything — whose one piece of feedback was a word in the
362	// header, which is precisely where Rule 136 says a filter does not go. The
363	// ports tab already had the mechanism; this is the same one.
364	//
365	// There are four rather than one per docker state because the mapping has to be
366	// total: a state named by no token would be a container hidden with nothing on
367	// screen saying which filter hid it. They are exactly the four groups
368	// containerStateStyle already colours, so the bar and the status column say the
369	// same thing.
370	const (
371		filterTokenRunning   = "running"
372		filterTokenPaused    = "paused"
373		filterTokenStopped   = "stopped"
374		filterTokenTransient = "transient"
375	)
376	
377	// stateTokens is the declaration order, which is the order the bar shows them
378	// in and the order `z` walks to clear them.
379	var stateTokens = []string{
380		filterTokenRunning, filterTokenPaused, filterTokenStopped, filterTokenTransient,
381	}
382	
383	// defaultStateToken is what an empty selection shows.
384	//
385	// It is the view's resting state rather than a token that starts lit: a lit
386	// token keeps the filter bar on screen from the first frame, and the bar is not
387	// the point — the running containers are. So the view opens with no token, the
388	// bar hidden, and this is the set. `z` returns here, which is why arriving and
389	// pressing `z` now land on the same screen instead of two different ones.
390	//
391	// The cost, stated rather than discovered: the opening scope is not written
392	// anywhere on screen. It is the one thing the old `a` got wrong, and it is kept
393	// on purpose — the difference is that the moment the user has an opinion, the
394	// bar appears and names every state it is showing, which `a` never did.
395	const defaultStateToken = REDACTED
396	
397	// stateToken names the token a docker state belongs to.
398	//
399	// The default branch is what makes it total: `exited` and `dead` land there
400	// today, and so does anything docker starts reporting tomorrow — a state the
401	// application does not recognise still belongs to a container that is not
402	// running, which is a row the user can reach rather than one that has vanished.
403	func stateToken(state string) string {
404		switch state {
405		case "running":
406			return filterTokenRunning
407		case "paused":
408			return filterTokenPaused
409		case "created", "restarting", "removing":
410			return filterTokenTransient
411		default: // exited, dead, and whatever comes next
412			return filterTokenStopped
413		}
414	}
415	
416	// matchContainerTokens applies the state filter: OR between the tokens that are
417	// on, and defaultStateToken when none of them is.
418	//
419	// The empty selection is the view's default rather than "everything", which is
420	// where this parts company with the ports tab: there, nothing on means no
421	// opinion and shows every socket. Here the resting state is an opinion — the
422	// running containers — and it has to be, because it is what keeps the bar
423	// hidden on arrival. "Everything" is therefore the four tokens together, which
424	// is what it literally is; there is no `all` token, because that would be a
425	// fifth state to select alongside four real ones.
426	func matchContainerTokens(c docker.Container, active map[string]bool) bool {
427		token := stateToken(c.State)
428		anyOn := false
429		for _, label := range stateTokens {
430			if !active[label] {
431				continue
432			}
433			anyOn = true
434			if token == label {
435				return true
436			}
437		}
438		if anyOn {
439			return false
440		}
441		return token == defaultStateToken

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case " ":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case " ":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

</system-reminder>

# TUI — Theme, Colors & Background

### Rule 102 : Centralized management of colors and styles

- All colors must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`
- Never hardcode colors directly in views
- Reusable styles must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/styles.go`
- Use the theme package's constants (ColorPrimary, ColorError, etc.)

### Rule 105 : Help message format

- Standard format: `[key] action  [key] action`
- Displayed with `theme.HelpStyle` (italic + ColorDim)
- Keys in square brackets `[]`
- Separated by at least 2 spaces

### Rule 115 : Uniform background handling (lipgloss)

**lipgloss does NOT propagate a parent's background to its children.**

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` insert "bare" spaces that show the terminal's native background.

| Forbidden | Alternative |
|----------|-------------|
| `lipgloss.JoinHorizontal` to assemble blocks | Build each line manually with `PadWithBg()` |
| `lipgloss.JoinVertical` to stack lines | `strings.Join(lines, "\n")` with each line padded |
| `strings.Repeat("\n", n)` for blank lines | `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` |
| `lipgloss.NewStyle().Render(text)` with no background | `.Background(ColorBackground)` mandatory |
| Hardcoded hex color | Global variables (`ColorBackground`, `ColorDim`, etc.) |

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` are acceptable **only** if the result is wrapped in a `.Background(ColorBackground).Width(w)` style.

`lipgloss.Place` → always use `WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground)`.

**Drawing over an already rendered screen** (the command palette) goes through
`overlay.Compose` (`internal/ui/overlay`) and nothing else: it splices with
`x/ansi` and never cuts an escape sequence. `lipgloss.Place` stays for full-screen
modals. Never slice a styled line by bytes or runes.

### Rule 117 : Centralized helpers of the `theme` package

**Never recreate `bg()`, `padWithBg()`, `bgWrap()` locally.**

| Function | Usage |
|----------|-------|
| `theme.Bg(s)` | Plain text with the app background |
| `theme.PadWithBg(content, width)` | Pad up to `width` with background |
| `theme.BgLine(s, width)` | Text + background + pad up to `width` |
| `theme.BgWrap(s, width)` | Background + pad on each line (multi-line) |
| `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` | Blank line filled with background |
| `theme.OverlayBoxStyle()` | Standard style for overlay modals |
| `overlay.Compose(base, box, x, y, width)` | Box drawn over rendered lines, ANSI-safe |

- **Inline text** → `theme.Bg("text")`
- **Full line** → `theme.BgLine("text", width)`
- **Multi-line paragraph** → `theme.BgWrap(text, width)`
- **Blank line** → `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)`
- **Modal overlay** → `theme.OverlayBoxStyle().Render(content)`

### Rule 118 : Standardizing table and tab colors

| Element | Foreground | Background |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Table header | `ColorSecondary` | — |
| Selected row (normal) | **each column's own** | `ColorTableLineSelected`, bold |
| Selected row (error) | `ColorBlack` | `ColorError` |
| Active tab | `ColorBlack` | `ColorSecondary` |
| Inactive tab | `ColorDim` | `ColorCommandLineBg` |

**Selected row (normal)** (§3.72 in the backlog; confirmed 2026-09-21). It used to
be one flat `ColorBlack` on `ColorSecondary`, dropping every column's own
colour — see Rule 122's "Selected row" section for why that used to be
mandatory and why it no longer is for this one variant: every cell now
repaints `ColorTableLineSelected` and bold **itself**, which is what makes
keeping the per-cell foreground safe instead of a return of the defect.
`error`, `busy` (`TableStylesForState`) and severity
(`TableStylesForSeverity`) are untouched — a solid background there still
means "this whole row is in that state," which per-cell colour would fight.

`ColorTableLineSelected` (`table_line_selected` in a theme file) is its own
key rather than an alias of `ColorSeverityLow`, on purpose: `ColorSeverityLow`
now points at the same tone as `ColorDim` — the colour the `:sec` inventory
already uses for a "0" count (Rule 122's "Color discipline") — so a theme
tuning "how muted is a LOW finding" no longer also retunes the selection
highlight by coincidence. Both keys default to the same hex the "normal"
selection has always used, so nothing changes on screen from this split by
itself.

Mandatory centralized functions:
- `theme.DefaultTableStyles()` — base style
- `theme.TableStylesForState(state)` — `"normal"` or `"error"`
- `theme.TableStylesForSeverity(severity)` — `"CRITICAL"`, `"HIGH"`, `"MEDIUM"`, `"LOW"`, `"UNKNOWN"`

Forbidden:
- ❌ Selection styles defined locally in views
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for active tabs or headers (use `ColorSecondary`)

### Rule 119 : No hardcoded hex color outside `colors.go`

**`lipgloss.Color("#...")` must appear ONLY in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`.**

3-level architecture:

| Level | File | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| **1. Base palette** | `colors.go` lines 6-32 | Raw hex colors (Catppuccin) |
| **2. Semantic colors** | `colors.go` lines 34+ | Aliases by usage, referencing the palette |
| **3. Styles** | `styles.go`, views | lipgloss styles using the semantic colors |

If a hex color is needed with no semantic equivalent:
1. Add it to the base palette (`colors.go`, hex section)
2. Create a semantic alias that references the palette

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
var ColorMaroon = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // dans palette de base
ColorSeverityHigh = ColorMaroon              // in the semantic section

// ❌ WRONG
ColorSeverityHigh = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // hardcoded hex in the semantic section
```

`manager.go`'s fallbacks → reference `colors.go`, never hex values.

### Rule 127 : Relative time — `theme.TimeAgo`

**Every view displaying a relative time must use `theme.TimeAgo(t time.Time) string`** (`internal/ui/theme/timeago.go`).

| Duration | Output |
|-------|--------|
| < 1 min | `"now"` |
| < 1 hour | `"59 min ago"` |
| < 24 h | `"23 hr ago"` |
| < 30 days | `"30 days ago"` |
| < 12 months | `"11 mo ago"` |
| else | `"99 yr ago"` |
| zero | `""` |

Forbidden: local implementations, long formats, compact with no space.

### Rule 129 : Interface and log language — English US only

**All UI text and all logs must be in American English.**

| Category | Rule |
|-----------|-------|
| Labels, titles, UI messages | ✅ English US |
| Error messages (footer) | ✅ English US |
| Help (`GetHelpContent`, `GetShortcuts`) | ✅ English US |
| Cell values, empty messages | ✅ English US |
| Logs (`log.Printf`) | ✅ English US |
| Code comments | ✅ English only (Rule 307) |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Loading workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Failed to refresh — check logs"

// ❌ WRONG
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Chargement des workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Échec du rafraîchissement — voir les logs"
```

theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Chargement des workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Échec du rafraîchissement — voir les logs"
```

# TUI — Theme, Colors & Background

### Rule 102 : Centralized management of colors and styles

- All colors must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`
- Never hardcode colors directly in views
- Reusable styles must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/styles.go`
- Use the theme package's constants (ColorPrimary, ColorError, etc.)

### Rule 105 : Help message format

- Standard format: `[key] action  [key] action`
- Displayed with `theme.HelpStyle` (italic + ColorDim)
- Keys in square brackets `[]`
- Separated by at least 2 spaces

### Rule 115 : Uniform background handling (lipgloss)

**lipgloss does NOT propagate a parent's background to its children.**

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` insert "bare" spaces that show the terminal's native background.

| Forbidden | Alternative |
|----------|-------------|
| `lipgloss.JoinHorizontal` to assemble blocks | Build each line manually with `PadWithBg()` |
| `lipgloss.JoinVertical` to stack lines | `strings.Join(lines, "\n")` with each line padded |
| `strings.Repeat("\n", n)` for blank lines | `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` |
| `lipgloss.NewStyle().Render(text)` with no background | `.Background(ColorBackground)` mandatory |
| Hardcoded hex color | Global variables (`ColorBackground`, `ColorDim`, etc.) |

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` are acceptable **only** if the result is wrapped in a `.Background(ColorBackground).Width(w)` style.

`lipgloss.Place` → always use `WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground)`.

**Drawing over an already rendered screen** (the command palette) goes through
`overlay.Compose` (`internal/ui/overlay`) and nothing else: it splices with
`x/ansi` and never cuts an escape sequence. `lipgloss.Place` stays for full-screen
modals. Never slice a styled line by bytes or runes.

### Rule 117 : Centralized helpers of the `theme` package

**Never recreate `bg()`, `padWithBg()`, `bgWrap()` locally.**

| Function | Usage |
|----------|-------|
| `theme.Bg(s)` | Plain text with the app background |
| `theme.PadWithBg(content, width)` | Pad up to `width` with background |
| `theme.BgLine(s, width)` | Text + background + pad up to `width` |
| `theme.BgWrap(s, width)` | Background + pad on each line (multi-line) |
| `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` | Blank line filled with background |
| `theme.OverlayBoxStyle()` | Standard style for overlay modals |
| `overlay.Compose(base, box, x, y, width)` | Box drawn over rendered lines, ANSI-safe |

- **Inline text** → `theme.Bg("text")`
- **Full line** → `theme.BgLine("text", width)`
- **Multi-line paragraph** → `theme.BgWrap(text, width)`
- **Blank line** → `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)`
- **Modal overlay** → `theme.OverlayBoxStyle().Render(content)`

### Rule 118 : Standardizing table and tab colors

| Element | Foreground | Background |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Table header | `ColorSecondary` | — |
| Selected row (normal) | **each column's own** | `ColorTableLineSelected`, bold |
| Selected row (error) | `ColorBlack` | `ColorError` |
| Active tab | `ColorBlack` | `ColorSecondary` |
| Inactive tab | `ColorDim` | `ColorCommandLineBg` |

**Selected row (normal)** (§3.72 in the backlog; confirmed 2026-09-21). It used to
be one flat `ColorBlack` on `ColorSecondary`, dropping every column's own
colour — see Rule 122's "Selected row" section for why that used to be
mandatory and why it no longer is for this one variant: every cell now
repaints `ColorTableLineSelected` and bold **itself**, which is what makes
keeping the per-cell foreground safe instead of a return of the defect.
`error`, `busy` (`TableStylesForState`) and severity
(`TableStylesForSeverity`) are untouched — a solid background there still
means "this whole row is in that state," which per-cell colour would fight.

`ColorTableLineSelected` (`table_line_selected` in a theme file) is its own
key rather than an alias of `ColorSeverityLow`, on purpose: `ColorSeverityLow`
now points at the same tone as `ColorDim` — the colour the `:sec` inventory
already uses for a "0" count (Rule 122's "Color discipline") — so a theme
tuning "how muted is a LOW finding" no longer also retunes the selection
highlight by coincidence. Both keys default to the same hex the "normal"
selection has always used, so nothing changes on screen from this split by
itself.

Mandatory centralized functions:
- `theme.DefaultTableStyles()` — base style
- `theme.TableStylesForState(state)` — `"normal"` or `"error"`
- `theme.TableStylesForSeverity(severity)` — `"CRITICAL"`, `"HIGH"`, `"MEDIUM"`, `"LOW"`, `"UNKNOWN"`

Forbidden:
- ❌ Selection styles defined locally in views
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for active tabs or headers (use `ColorSecondary`)

### Rule 119 : No hardcoded hex color outside `colors.go`

**`lipgloss.Color("#...")` must appear ONLY in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`.**

3-level architecture:

| Level | File | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| **1. Base palette** | `colors.go` lines 6-32 | Raw hex colors (Catppuccin) |
| **2. Semantic colors** | `colors.go` lines 34+ | Aliases by usage, referencing the palette |
| **3. Styles** | `styles.go`, views | lipgloss styles using the semantic colors |

If a hex color is needed with no semantic equivalent:
1. Add it to the base palette (`colors.go`, hex section)
2. Create a semantic alias that references the palette

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
var ColorMaroon = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // dans palette de base
ColorSeverityHigh = ColorMaroon              // in the semantic section

// ❌ WRONG
ColorSeverityHigh = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // hardcoded hex in the semantic section
```

`manager.go`'s fallbacks → reference `colors.go`, never hex values.

### Rule 127 : Relative time — `theme.TimeAgo`

**Every view displaying a relative time must use `theme.TimeAgo(t time.Time) string`** (`internal/ui/theme/timeago.go`).

| Duration | Output |
|-------|--------|
| < 1 min | `"now"` |
| < 1 hour | `"59 min ago"` |
| < 24 h | `"23 hr ago"` |
| < 30 days | `"30 days ago"` |
| < 12 months | `"11 mo ago"` |
| else | `"99 yr ago"` |
| zero | `""` |

Forbidden: local implementations, long formats, compact with no space.

### Rule 129 : Interface and log language — English US only

**All UI text and all logs must be in American English.**

| Category | Rule |
|-----------|-------|
| Labels, titles, UI messages | ✅ English US |
| Error messages (footer) | ✅ English US |
| Help (`GetHelpContent`, `GetShortcuts`) | ✅ English US |
| Cell values, empty messages | ✅ English US |
| Logs (`log.Printf`) | ✅ English US |
| Code comments | ✅ English only (Rule 307) |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Loading workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Failed to refresh — check logs"

// ❌ WRONG
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Chargement des workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Échec du rafraîchissement — voir les logs"
```
